references.text: The original command on how the belt of the ephod was to be made, using the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, crimson wool, and twisted fine linen.
The description of the ephod itself, of which the belt was to be a part, made from the same materials.
The immediate context describing the making of the ephod with the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, crimson wool, and twisted fine linen.
Another example of skilled craftsmanship in the tabernacle using similar materials, showing consistency in construction.
The introduction to the section on priestly garments, which mentions the same colored materials used for holy clothing.
A parallel phrase 'as the Lord had commanded Moses' that is repeated throughout the chapter to show obedience to God's instructions.
Another example of the use of twisted fine linen and colored fabrics in the priestly garments, with the same formula of obedience.
